about: Eval tasks for the data library (stage 3). Same method as architecture.json and security.json: context coverage (pack vs pack+refs) is an availability proxy, not proof of better answers; rubric and refs share an author. Score real agent answers with --responses DIR.

tasks.prompt: Add a required `country_code` column to our 40-million-row `customers` table in Postgres without downtime.

rubric.text: expand/contract across releases
add nullable first, backfill in batches
CHECK (... IS NOT NULL) NOT VALID, then VALIDATE, then SET NOT NULL uses it
VALIDATE takes a weaker lock (SHARE UPDATE EXCLUSIVE)
set lock_timeout so a blocked ALTER does not queue everyone
lock queue: waiting ACCESS EXCLUSIVE blocks later readers

tasks.prompt: Write an Alembic migration that adds an index on orders(customer_id, created_at).

rubric.text: CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY
outside a transaction: autocommit_block in Alembic
a failed concurrent build leaves an INVALID index to drop and retry
equality column first, range/sort column second
lint the generated SQL (alembic --sql + squawk)

tasks.prompt: Design the tables for a mobile-money wallet (XAF and EUR) with deposits, transfers and fees.

rubric.text: integer minor units (bigint) or numeric, never float
store the currency code with every amount
XAF has zero decimal places
append-only double-entry ledger entries that sum to zero
balance derived or cached with a check, not the source of truth
idempotency key unique per request

tasks.prompt: Should our new Postgres tables use serial ids, UUIDv4, UUIDv7 or ULIDs?

rubric.text: bigint GENERATED ... AS IDENTITY rather than serial
UUIDv7 is time-ordered, good index locality
PostgreSQL 18 has uuidv7()
v7 embeds creation time; don't expose where that leaks information
UUIDv4 random inserts scatter the B-tree

tasks.prompt: We are turning our single-company app into SaaS for many schools. How should we separate tenant data in Postgres?

rubric.text: shared tables with tenant_id as the default
row-level security as a backstop
table owners and BYPASSRLS roles skip policies; use FORCE or a non-owner role
set the tenant per transaction (SET LOCAL / set_config(..., true)) with pooling
tenant_id leading in composite keys/indexes
schema- or database-per-tenant trade-offs

tasks.prompt: This orders list endpoint takes 4 seconds in production. Here is the query. Make it fast.

rubric.text: EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS) on production-like data
compare estimated vs actual rows
keyset pagination instead of large OFFSET
pg_stat_statements to find the worst queries
check for N+1 from the ORM
partial or covering index when it fits

tasks.prompt: Two staff members sometimes book the same room for overlapping times. Fix it in the database.

rubric.text: exclusion constraint on a range (btree_gist) or WITHOUT OVERLAPS
check-then-insert is a race (write skew) under READ COMMITTED
SERIALIZABLE needs retry on 40001
SELECT ... FOR UPDATE locks only existing rows
retry loop for serialization/deadlock errors

tasks.prompt: Our Postgres disk keeps growing although row counts are stable, and queries got slower. What is going on and what do we do?

rubric.text: MVCC dead tuples need vacuum
long-running or idle-in-transaction sessions block cleanup
autovacuum scale factor / per-table tuning
transaction ID wraparound risk
VACUUM FULL takes ACCESS EXCLUSIVE; prefer pg_repack-style tools

tasks.prompt: We get 'too many clients already' errors after scaling our API to 30 containers. Fix the database connections.

rubric.text: PgBouncer (or a managed pooler) in transaction mode
max_connections default is typically 100
transaction mode breaks session state (SET, advisory locks, LISTEN)
prepared statements need PgBouncer 1.21+ max_prepared_statements
size app pools so containers x pool fits the server

tasks.prompt: Set up backups for our production Postgres so we can recover from someone deleting a table.

rubric.text: base backup + WAL archiving for point-in-time recovery
pg_dump alone is a snapshot, not PITR
test restores regularly
a replica is not a backup (replicates the DROP)
RPO/RTO targets

tasks.prompt: Review this SQLAlchemy 2 FastAPI service: list endpoints are slow and tests use SQLite.

rubric.text: selectinload/joinedload to fix N+1
lazy='raise' to catch accidental lazy loads
test against real Postgres (testcontainers), not SQLite
expire_on_commit / async session pitfalls
factories over shared fixtures; never production data

tasks.prompt: Add product search with typo tolerance and cache popular product pages in Redis.

rubric.text: Postgres FTS (tsvector + GIN) first; dedicated engine when relevance/typos/facets demand it
pg_trgm for typo-tolerant similarity
TTL on every cache key
set maxmemory-policy (default noeviction)
invalidate on write / stampede protection
Redis is not the system of record

tasks.prompt: A user asked us to delete their account and data. We use soft delete everywhere. What should happen?

rubric.text: soft delete is not erasure
retention schedule per data class with a job that enforces it
backups and logs/analytics copies are part of the plan
keep legally required records (ledger) but pseudonymise personal fields
audit trail of the deletion itself

tasks.prompt: Management wants dashboards over all transactions. Can we just run the reports on the production database?

rubric.text: separate OLAP from OLTP (replica or warehouse)
change data capture / logical replication to feed it
materialized views; REFRESH CONCURRENTLY needs a unique index
replica queries can be cancelled or delay cleanup (hot_standby_feedback)
minimise PII in the analytics copy
